 Central Notes: Giannis, Haliburton, Giddey, Williams, Holland
 By Dana Gauruder |
 at November 17, 2026 5:40 pm 
 Giannis Antetokounmpo will face his former team for the first time on Wednesday in Miami. The Heat forward claims it will be business as usual when he faces the Bucks .
 “It’s going to be just another game ,” Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic’s Eric Nehm . “I’m going to do the same thing. I’m going to eat the same meal. I’m going to kiss my kids before they go to bed, get ready, wake up, do my routine and get ready for the game. It’s the same game. It’s the same thing. It doesn’t change. It doesn’t matter t he jersey.”
 The former MVP says he has little trouble separating his emotions from his on-court duties.
 “I haven’t found myself being emotional,” Antetokounmpo said. “I think the only time I’ve been emotional was when we won the championship. I think I’ve played my whole career, I haven’t found myself putting emotion into the game. I feel emotions are for movies, and this is just basketball. I’m gonna do prep, get my body ready and get ready for the game.” 
 We have more from the Central Division:
 It’s possible that Tyrese Haliburton could return before the end of the month, Pacers coach Rick Carlisle revealed during a 107.5 The Fan interview ( Twitter link ). Haliburton has only appeared in four games due to a left hamstring strain. “He’s getting there. At some point, somebody’s gonna ask, ‘Hey, is there any way he’ll play in November?’ I don’t think it’s out of the question, but we’re not in the position to put a hard date (on it),” Carlisle said.
 Josh Giddey is in the second year of a four-year, $100MM contract but he may be playing his way out of the starting point guard spot for the Bulls . Through 13 games, Giddey is averaging 9.9 points, 5.8 rebounds and 8.5 assists, shooting 40.7 percent from the field and 32 percent from 3-point range. Among the 154 players who’ve logged at least 300 minutes this season, Giddey ranks 91st in usage percentage, yet he ranks 13th in the NBA in turnover percentage among that group, The Athletic’s Joel Lorenzi points out. Giddey was benched for most of the fourth quarter against Cleveland on Monday. “I mean, I would have done the same thing if I was (coach Tiago Splitter ,” Giddey said. “ So, no, I’m not sitting there confused why I wasn’t playing down the stretch. It’s his call. It’s the right call.” 
 Until a scoreless 13-minute clunker on Monday, Bulls forward Patrick Williams had seen his minutes increase in recent games. Williams said he never lost his spirit when he was out of the rotation earlier this season, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network tweets . “Th e work relieves doubts,” Williams said. “And giving yourself to the team means you don’t have a chance to worry about yourself. I tried to be wise about being out of the rotation. Everyone goes through adversity. How you handle that shows who you are.” 
 Pistons swingman Ron Holland won’t play against the Spurs tonight due to a left knee contusion and bone bruise. However, Holland has shown growth in his game this season, Omari Sankofa II of the Detroit Free Press notes. Through 12 games, Holland has 22 assists and 11 turnovers – a 2-to-1 assist-to-turnover ratio. Last season, it was essentially a 1-to-1 ratio. “A l ot of it is just reading the floor,” said Holland, who is eligible for a rookie scale extension next offseason. “Sometimes in the past few seasons, I would get the ball and not know what to do with it or get the board and try to force something that’s not there.  But now it’s just, like, I’m learning that time is slow. Like, 3 seconds is a really long time, even if I get a messed-up pass or something, I’m able to just slow my mind down and make the right decision, make the easy decision.”
